title: DynamoDB NoSQL Database
description: Learn to design DynamoDB tables with partition and sort keys, use secondary indexes, and apply advanced features like Streams, TTL, and global tables.

data.text: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database. Unlike relational databases that store data in rows and columns, DynamoDB stores data as key-value pairs and documents. It is designed for single-digit millisecond performance at any scale.
A DynamoDB table is a collection of items. Each item is a group of attributes (like columns in a relational database). Every item must have a primary key that uniquely identifies it.
Primary Keys: Partition Key and Sort Key

data.title: Primary Key Types
items: **Simple primary key** — only a partition key. DynamoDB uses the partition key's value to determine where to store the item.
**Composite primary key** — a partition key plus a sort key. Items with the same partition key are stored together and sorted by the sort key.

data.title: Designing Keys
data.text: Choose a partition key with many distinct values to distribute data evenly across partitions. Use the sort key when you need to query items in a specific order.
A Query operation finds items using the primary key. It is efficient and uses indexes. A Scan operation reads every item in the table. Scans are expensive and should be avoided in production.

Global Secondary Indexes (GSI) let you query on non-primary key attributes. You can add or delete a GSI at any time. Local Secondary Indexes (LSI) use the same partition key as the base table but a different sort key. LSIs must be created when the table is created.
Streams, TTL, Global Tables, and DAX

data.title: Advanced Features
items: **DynamoDB Streams** — captures a time-ordered sequence of changes (insert, update, delete) for use with Lambda triggers
**TTL** — automatically deletes items after a specified timestamp, useful for session data or temporary records
**Global Tables** — fully managed, multi-region, multi-active database that replicates changes across Regions
**DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator)** — an in-memory cache that reduces response times from milliseconds to microseconds

terms.definition: The primary attribute that determines where a DynamoDB item is stored. All items with the same partition key are stored together.
An optional secondary key that sorts items with the same partition key in ascending order.
An index with a partition key and optional sort key that can be different from the base table's keys.
A time-ordered log of changes to items in a DynamoDB table, often used with Lambda for real-time processing.
DynamoDB Accelerator, a fully managed in-memory cache that improves read performance for frequently accessed items.

data.title: Design a DynamoDB Table
data.description: Create a DynamoDB table for a blog application. Your table should store posts and comments efficiently.
steps: Decide on a partition key strategy for posts
Decide on a sort key strategy if using a composite key
Identify which queries your application needs (e.g., get post by ID, get comments by post)
Create GSI for alternative access patterns
Enable TTL for expired comment drafts
data.expectedOutcome: A clear data model with primary key design, GSIs, and rationale for your choices.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond performance
Use a partition key and optional sort key for the primary key
Queries are efficient; scans are expensive and should be avoided
GSIs let you query on non-key attributes; TTL auto-expires items
data.takeaway: DynamoDB excels at scale. Design your keys carefully, and you can handle millions of requests with no servers to manage.
